newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss parliament to decide on revalued gold sales.
newsitem.headline: Swiss parliament to decide on revalued gold sales.

text.p: Switzerland's parliament will decide what to do with official gold reserves that are revalued but not given to a proposed seven billion Swiss franc humanitarian foundation, a finance ministry official said on Friday.

Finance Ministry director Ulrich Gygi also told a news briefing that the government was in no hurry to sell gold reserves other than those given to the foundation that are supposed to be revalued next year in line with a plan announced on Wednesday.

The Swiss government proposed selling revalued offical gold reserves to finance the seven billion Swiss franc humanitarian fund. Swiss National Bank Chairman Hans Meyer has said the foundation could sell the gold it gets over 10 years to avoid market disruptions.

The revaluation planned for next year would increase Swiss gold reserves by around 14 billion francs, half of which would be transferred to the foundation under the plan, which still needs legislative approval and will be subject to at least one referendum.

Asked what the government planned to do with the remaining seven billion in revalued gold, Gygi said a number of proposals were taking shape in parliament for uses ranging from deficit reduction to social security. "It is up to parliament to decide what to do with the profit from revaluation," he said, but added there was no need to sell the gold quickly.
"As for the second tranche of gains from the revaluation, there is no need to realise its value immediately by selling it," he said. "We will be able to wait for the market" to develop, he added.
